findings.trigger: During the confirmation ladder for a start/stop/restart (single container or a group), one target's status fetch fails on an attempt (`status.success` is False, e.g. a transient Docker error) while every OTHER target already shows the wanted state. The failing target is skipped with `continue` (line 122) and is never appended to `running` (line 123), so `running` is shorter than `targets`. `_has_taken_effect(action, running)` (line 67, called at line 132) only asks whether every entry IN `running` matches - it has no idea an entry is missing - so `all(running)` (start/restart) or `not any(running)` (stop) is satisfied by the confirmed subset alone, and `wait_until_the_action_took_effect` returns True even though the failing member's real state was never confirmed on that attempt.
findings.suggestion: Treat a failed status fetch as "not yet confirmed" for that attempt instead of dropping the target: e.g. append a sentinel/None to `running` (or track len(targets) vs len(running)) and let `_has_taken_effect` require both counts to match, so one member whose status could not be read keeps the ladder going (or ends in the honest False/None instead of True).

findings.trigger: Calling `validate_custom_address` with an IPv6 address such as `::1` or `fe80::1`: `address.rpartition(':')` splits at the LAST colon, so `host` still contains colons (e.g. `::` or `fe80::`) and `port` is read from the trailing digit group (e.g. `1`, which passes `validate_custom_port`). `host` then fails both the IPv4 pattern and the hostname pattern (`^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+$`, no colons allowed) and the function returns False for every IPv6 address, including ones with no port at all.
findings.suggestion: If IPv6 custom addresses are meant to be settable, add an IPv6-aware branch (and decide how a bracketed `[::1]:8080`-style port suffix is written); if IPv6 is intentionally out of scope, no change is needed - this is reported because I could not tell which from the material given.
findings.unsure_why: SPEC.md does not say whether DDC's custom address field is meant to accept IPv6 at all, and the two callers that build the full address+port string (control_ui.py, status_info_integration.py) are outside this section, so I cannot see whether IPv6 is ever offered to the user in practice.

notes: cogs/admin_overview.py and cogs/stack_restart.py carry extensive in-code comments that pre-empt exactly the two most obvious-looking 'findings' in this area (no channel check on the bulk/admin buttons - deliberate per SPEC B2, pinned by tests/spec/test_the_bulk_buttons_answer_to_the_admin_list.py) - confirmed against SPEC.md, not reported. Two duplicated-logic observations, neither a live bug: (1) admin_overview.py's `_restart_summary` (163-174) and the inline description built in `ConfirmStopAllButton.callback` (932-942) construct the same kind of bulk-result text by two separate code paths instead of one shared helper; currently they agree line for line, so this is a drift risk, not a finding. (2) `stack_restart.py`'s `ConfirmRestartStackButton.callback` (293-294) narrows `members` to what `admin_service.controllable()` returns and computes `not_touched` via `m not in allowed`, a dict-equality membership test; `admin_service` itself is outside this section so I could not confirm whether `controllable()` returns the same dict objects/values it was given (if it ever normalises or copies entries differently, the `not in` check could miscount) - flagged here only as something depending on code I cannot see, not as a finding. cogs/__init__.py (7 lines) contains no public names from PLAN.txt and had nothing to check.
